key_insight: Homogeneous, fully alloyed WC–Co–Cr powder enables dense, layered cermet coatings, while spray method selection trades off hardness and tribological performance.
engineering_relevance: The results help optimize WC–Co–Cr coating processing for wear-resistant machine parts operating under high friction and high load.
method: Compared HVOF and detonation spraying for WC–Co–Cr cermet deposition.
Characterized powder morphology, coating microstructure, and phase composition using SEM and EDS.
Evaluated hardness, density, and friction behavior to relate processing to performance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a higher average microhardness for detonation-sprayed coatings (1449 HV) and a low friction coefficient for HVOF coatings (Kt = 0.143).
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on powder quality and spray parameters, so the reported results may not transfer directly to other feedstock morphologies or operating conditions.
paper_title: INVESTIGATION OF THE FORMATION OF STRUCTURE AND WEAR-RESISTANT PROPERTIES OF WC–CO–CR COATINGS PRODUCED BY HVOF AND DETONATION SPRAYING
